newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at an intraday low of 8.2925 against the U.S. dollar on Monday from a two-year high of 8.2910 last Friday due to profit-taking, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2915.
Dealers said profit-taking emerged in late trading on Monday after the yuan's solid gains last Friday.
The yuan opened up at an intraday high of 8.2905 and fell slightly to move around 8.2915 for most of the session, before slipping further in the last fifteen minutes of trading, traders said.
Trading was dull early in the session but active late in the session with most business done at 8.2915, traders said.
One dealer said after the yuan hit a two-year high last Friday, it needed a technical correction on Monday.
"The yuan faced selling pressure when it approached the key 8.2900 resistance level after opening higher, indicating a technical correction was needed after Friday's gains," he said.
A second dealer said profit-taking offers were seen at around the 8.2920 level late in trading, forcing the yuan down.
"The yuan is expected to move around the 8.2920 level in the next few days with no fresh market-moving factors around the corner," he said.
Traders said they expected the yuan to edge up on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at 7.1770 from 7.2510 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0704 from 1.0705 against the Hong Kong dollar.
